Executive Order 11329
CREATING A BOARD OF INQUIRY TO REPORT ON A LABOR DISPUTE
AFFECTING THE SHIPBUILDING AND REPAIR INDUSTRIES OF THE
UNITED STATES
W H E R E A S , there exists a labor dispute between the Pacific Coast 
Shipbuilders’ Association, Alameda, California, representing Lock­
heed Shipbuilding and Construction Company, Seattle, Washington,  
Bethlehem Steel Company, San Francisco, California, Lake Union  
Dry Docks Company, Seattle, Washington, Pacific Coast Engineering  
Company, Alameda, California, Albina Engine and Machine Works,  
Portland, Oregon, Northwest Marine Iron Works, Portland, Oregon,  
Todd Shipyards Corporation, Seattle, Washington and Alameda,  
California, Guy F. Atkinson Company, Portland, Oregon, Willamette  
Iron and Steel Company, Portland, Oregon, and certain of their em­
ployees represented by the International Brotherhood of Electrical  
Workers, A F L -C I O ; and
W H E R E A S , such dispute has resulted in a strike which will, in my 
opinion, if permitted to continue, affect a substantial part of the ship­
building and repair industries, which industries are engaged in trade,  
commerce, transportation, transmission, or communication among the  
several States or with foreign nations, or engaged m the production of  
goods for commerce, and which strike, if permitted to continue, will  
imperil the national safety:
N O W  T H E R E F O R E , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act of 1947 (61 Stat.  
155: 29 U.S.C. 176),H  hereby create a Board of Inquiry, consisting of  
Mr. J. Keith Mann, Chairman, Mr. George E. Reedy and Mr. Paul D.  
Hanlon, whom I  appoint to inquire into the issues involved m this
dispute.
The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title I I  of  
such Act. The Board shall report to the President m accordance  
with the provisions of Section 206 of such Act on or before March 8,

1967.
Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence  
to perform such other functions as may be required under such Act.

versions.research_rationale:
EO 11329 (1967-03-02, 32 FR 3811) creates a board of inquiry under section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act, 1947 to inquire into a labor dispute between the Pacific Coast Shipbuilders' Association members and employees represented by the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers affecting the shipbuilding and repair industries, appoints its named members, gives it the powers and duties of Title II of that Act, directs it to report on or before March 8, 1967, and provides that after its report the board continues in existence to perform other functions the Act requires. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11329.txt, 32 FR 3811, PDF pages 7-7). The dossier's inventory is incomplete or split mid-sentence (it omits the order's opening paragraphs or divides the report date from its year), so I replaced it with one clause covering the whole printed order from its heading to its last sentence. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25) revokes the order by number. The first end is that express revocation. The board's report date and any later discharge of the board are not established by a held reviewed source and are not ends. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order sets a report date ('report on or before March 8, 1967') and says the board continues in existence after reporting to perform functions required under the Act; it states no end date. A report date is a deadline, not an end. The board's actual report, any settlement and any discharge of the board under Title II of the Act are not established by a held reviewed source, so no earlier end is claimed. The by-number scan lists no held later order citing this order other than EO 12553, which names it; the catalog note, the U.S. Code and the eCFR searches add nothing earlier.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order creates the board, appoints its named members and sets its report date. The appointments are one-time acts whose surviving consequence (the members' service and the board's report) is a completed fact; no held source shows when the board was discharged, so no earlier end is asserted. The order creates no fund, delegation or continuing authority outside the board and survives only as long as the order does.","savings_check":"Savings: none in EO 12553 or in this order; the board's acts are completed facts and nothing continues independently of the order.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full; its table entry carries no 'in part' limit, so the single corrected clause ends on the revocation date. No held source records a partial amendment."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text), so the revocation leaves no part of this order in operation. The board's creation, appointments, report and any later discharge are completed facts whose dates are not held, and the order created no continuing right or fund.

first_end.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553: its operative sentence ends with the words "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and is followed by a two-column table headed 'No. Subject' whose entry "11329 Creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute affecting the shipbuilding and repair" names this order by number; EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the full held text was searched for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending), so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986). The signing-date reading is an inference from the order's heading and signature block, not express wording.
